question_text: Mary takes out a loan of $\$10\,000$ to purchase a car. The bank charges an interest rate of $8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Mary will repay the loan with quarterly repayments over 5 years.

mark_breakdown.desc: Entering TVM parameters with $N = 20, I\% = 8, PV = 10000, FV = 0, P/Y = 4, C/Y = 12$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: When payment frequency and compounding frequency differ, set $P/Y$ and $C/Y$ accordingly in the TVM solver ($P/Y = 4$, $C/Y = 12$).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Leaving $C/Y$ equal to $P/Y = 4$ when compounding is monthly ($C/Y = 12$).

subparts.stem: Find the balance of the loan after 3 years.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting $N = 12$ to find future value after 3 years

subparts.solution:
$N = 3 \times 4 = 12$, $I\% = 8$, $PV = 10\,000$, $\text{PMT} = -612.36$, $P/Y = 4$, $C/Y = 12$
$\therefore FV \approx -4483.17$
The balance of the loan is $\$4483.17$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The balance of a loan after $k$ periods is the future value $FV$ evaluated at $N = k$.
step_by_step: Solve for $FV \approx -4483.17$, meaning the balance is $\$4483.17$.

subparts.stem: After 3 years, Mary decided she would like to have the loan paid off in 1 year's time. What must her quarterly repayment increase to for this to occur?
subparts.solution:
$N = 1 \times 4 = 4$, $I\% = 8$, $PV = 4483.17$, $FV = 0$, $P/Y = 4$, $C/Y = 12$
$\therefore \text{PMT} \approx -1177.77$
The quarterly repayment must increase to $\$1177.77$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To pay off a loan earlier, set the new remaining term $N$ and use the current outstanding balance as $PV$ to recalculate the payment.
step_by_step: Solve for PMT: $\text{PMT} \approx -1177.77$, so the new repayment is $\$1177.77$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the remaining time originally scheduled (2 years, $N = 8$) instead of the accelerated timeframe of 1 year ($N = 4$).
